description: §41.12.1 rule 6 — a template the compiler cannot see (here a `const` string) is parsed by the runtime when registerMessages runs, with the same grammar and slot table, and FAILS CLOSED: `"{field} needs {threshold}"` names a slot LengthFailed does not have, so the second registration is refused, the first (well-formed, literal) template stays, and it renders — the unknown `{threshold}` is never shown as text and nothing renders half-filled. The compile reports no E-MESSAGE-* code (the bad template is not a literal).
rationale: §41.12.1 rule 6: a non-literal template that is malformed, names a slot its variant lacks, or is not a string is refused — not registered (an earlier registration for that variant, if any, stays), reported on the console, and the chain falls through. Asserting the EARLIER developer-authored template (rather than the Level-3 default, whose wording is impl-freedom) pins both halves: the refusal happened (the later template did not win) and the earlier entry survived it.
